To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the safety of the manipulatordesign is analyzed by an analytic worst-case estimation of the impact and clamping force in the absence of a collision detection system, that the evaluation shows that the worst case claming forces are only 25 N while the robot can handle loads up to two kg, that the effective mass in non near-singluar configurations is less than 0,4 kg and that the results are validated by simulation and experiments.
the BioRob arm design allows for safe human-robot interaction with a maximum of 25 N clamping forces, while being able, to handle loads up of 2 kg.

the BioRob manipulator is designed for safe physical humanrobot interaction, and that the safety evaluation shows that the manipulator is able to handle loads in the order of 2 kg, while constraining the worst case clapping forces to only 2 N.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a safe, lightweight, series-elastic, tendon-driven robot manipulator for safe physical human–robot interaction.
the safety of a novel, tendon-driven, series elastic robot arm for physical human-robot-interactions.
the design and safety analysis of a series elastic, lightweight, tendon-driven manipulator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BioRob design is a safe manipulator for physical human-robot interactions, as the worst case clamped force is below 25 N, and the impact forces are extremely low, even in the worst case.
the BioRob arm design is safe for physical human-robot-interactions.
the robot arm is safe in the sense of the safety criteria presented, but the safety of the robot arm in human-robot interactions cannot be guaranteed without a proper safety controller.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel lightweight, spring-loaded, tendon driven manipulator, and have evaluated its safety in case of collisions.
the BioRob manipulator is designed for safe physical human robot interaction and that its compliance can be controlled by a novel method for safe operation.

the design of the BioRob manipulator is safe and compliant enough to enable a human operator to interact with the robot arm in an intuitive way, while being able, to handle loads up-to 2 kg, which is the weight of an average human arm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a lightweight, series elastic actuator can be used to create a safe manipulator for human-robot interaction with a very low impact and clamping force.

the design of the BioRob arm allows for the development of a safe and compliant manipulator for physical human-robot-interactions, which can handle loads of 2 kg while constraining the worst case clamped force to 25 N.
a spring-loaded tendon-driven design can provide safe and compliant interaction with humans, and that a safety evaluation can be used to ensure that the design constraints are satisfied.
